name: Larimar
spiritual: Linked to water and the divine feminine
Said to carry the energy of Atlantis
physical: Traditionally associated with cooling and calming
Crystal healers link it with relaxation of the shoulders and throat
Folklore connects it with comfort during seasonal heat
Often kept nearby for restful sleep
summary: Larimar is the rare Caribbean blue stone of calm, ocean waves and emotional ease, found in only one place on Earth. Explore its meaning and care.
intro: Larimar is the colour of a shallow Caribbean lagoon, with swirls of white clouding through pale-to-vivid blue. It is a blue variety of pectolite, and in the whole world it is found in only one small area of the Dominican Republic. The cobalt-blue colour comes from copper replacing some of the calcium, and the white patterns are said to look like waves or drifting clouds. Cut cabochons often show a faint silky sheen, and pieces with deep, even blue and distinct white webbing command high prices. Holding one feels like holding a small piece of tropical sea.
history: Local people knew of the blue stone for generations, but the modern story begins in 1974, when a Dominican, Miguel Mendez, and a Peace Corps volunteer, Norman Rilling, rediscovered it. Rilling combined his daughter's name, Larissa, with the Spanish word for sea, mar, to coin larimar. The stone is mined from volcanic rock in the Barahona province, in small tunnels dug by hand. Some lore links it to the legendary lost city of Atlantis, though that is a modern metaphysical association rather than historical fact. It is now the national gemstone of the Dominican Republic.
meaning: Larimar is regarded as one of the most soothing stones in the crystal world. Its sea colours are linked to the throat and heart, encouraging calm, honest speech, and the release of tension held in the body. Practitioners use it for emotional flow, helping someone who feels stuck or overwhelmed to let feelings move like gentle waves. It is said to counter anger and fear with a sense of lightness. In meditation, it is associated with deep inner peace and the divine feminine. Some call it a dolphin stone because of its colour and the sense of play. Many keep it near when facing grief or heated situations that need a cool head.
howToUse: Hold a palm stone while breathing slowly, picturing gentle waves under a clear sky, to wind down after a stressful day. Wear it at the throat or on a bracelet for calm communication. Place a piece beside the bath, or on a shelf near the bed, for a spa-like atmosphere. In water-themed spaces, such as a bathroom, it feels at home. In a grid, use it with selenite and clear quartz for a soft, clearing layout. Since it can fade in strong light, display it out of direct sun.
care: Larimar is only moderately hard, so treat it kindly. A quick rinse in cool water is acceptable, but avoid hot water, steam, harsh chemicals and ultrasonic cleaners. Prolonged strong sunlight can fade the blue, so keep it out of the sun and charge it under moonlight instead. Cleanse with sound, smoke or by resting it on selenite. Wipe dry with a soft cloth and store separately in a pouch so harder stones cannot scratch it. Do not wear it in heavy exercise or hot tubs.
identify: Genuine larimar shows blue and white swirls and rarely looks uniform. It is found in only one place, so any claim of origin elsewhere is suspicious. Common fakes are blue-dyed howlite or calcite, blue glass, and resin-based composites, which often show repetitive patterns or overly even colour. Cheap strands sold as larimar are rarely genuine. A reputable seller will give grade and locality. Real larimar feels cool and heavier than plastic, and its colour sits within the pale sky to deep sea blue range.

faq.a: In crystal tradition, larimar is a calming stone linked to the throat and heart, used for emotional ease, gentle communication and meditation. These are traditional metaphysical associations, not medical claims.

Gem-quality larimar comes from a single mining area in the Barahona region of the Dominican Republic. This extreme rarity of source is one reason it is valued, and why claims of other origins should be questioned.

faq.q: Does larimar fade in the sun?
faq.a: Yes, prolonged strong sunlight and heat can fade larimar's blue colour. Keep it out of direct sun and charge it by moonlight. Brief exposure is unlikely to cause harm, but display it in shade to preserve its colour.
